name: Haditha–Baniyas Oil Pipeline

values.RouteType: Not mapped (but could be — route or endpoints are known)
values.RouteNotes: No official GIS/traced route found; the oil minister himself said (Peregraf, 2026-07-15) he 'did not provide a detailed map of the proposed northern route.' Endpoints are named and sourced (Haditha, Al Anbar, Iraq -> Baniyas Port, Syria), building off the Basra-Haditha trunk (P0544) as launch point per MEES -- point-A-to-point-B only, no coordinates/geometry.

researcher_notes:
Re-checked match-to-existing first: pulled all 86 existing Iraq oil rows from discovery_context.json. Two families sit near this candidate but are genuinely distinct: (1) Basra-Aqaba Oil Pipeline family (P0544 Basra-Haditha trunk, under construction; P5240 Haditha-Aqaba branch, proposed) -- same Haditha launch point but a different destination (Aqaba, Jordan, not Baniyas, Syria); thenationalnews (2026-05-01) explicitly names both as separate planned branches off the same trunk ('Ministry plans branches from Haditha toward Jordan (Aqaba) and toward Baniyas (Syria)'). (2) Kirkuk-Baniyas Oil Pipelines family (P0546/P5277/P5278/P5279/P7913) -- same Baniyas destination but a different, older origin (Kirkuk, not Haditha) and a wholly separate rehabilitation track: on 2026-07-16/17 Basra Oil Company's CEO and Syrian Petroleum Company's CEO signed a pact in Washington specifically to rehabilitate that OLD Kirkuk-Baniyas line (iraqinews, 'Iraq, Syria sign oil pipeline deal' -- explicitly 'revitalizing the Kirkuk-Baniyas pipeline'); that news updates the EXISTING P0546 family's status/notes, it is not evidence for this candidate and I did not use it as a ref here. Neither family covers a Haditha-origin line to Baniyas. Classed new_row, not matched_existing.

Add-threshold: (a) sponsor -- Iraq's Oil Ministry / state-owned Basra Oil Co, on the record: Iraq Business News (2026-01-28, sourced to 'Ministry of Oil') reports Oil Minister Hayan Abdul-Ghani chaired a review of the Haditha-Baniyas implementation plan; Peregraf (2026-07-15) quotes current Oil Minister Bassim Khudair by name describing 'a branch from Haditha to Syria's Baniyas' as part of the pipeline program a Chevron/Capital TI/UCC consortium would build. Used the existing 'Iraq Ministry of Oil' GEM entity (entity_lookup.py match, E100000000571) -- no new entity needed. (b) country + endpoints -- Iraq (Haditha, Al Anbar) to Syria (Baniyas) is named consistently across MEES, Iraq Business News, Peregraf, and IraqiNews. (c) concrete step -- Iraq's cabinet approved (5 Jul 2026) a heads-of-agreement + NDA between state-owned Basra Oil Co. and the Chevron/Capital TI/UCC Holding consortium naming the Basra-Haditha-Baniyas route as one of two feasibility-study comparison paths (Pipeline Technology Journal, 2026-07-06); this is a signed, cabinet-ratified agreement (functionally an MOU) with a named counterparty, clearing the SOP's 'MOU signed' bar even though it is explicitly described as non-binding/exploratory. All three legs clear.

Sources (>=2 independent, verified via url_verifier.py): (1) MEES (Middle East Economic Survey), 2026-01-30, direct trade-press reporting of the Oil Ministry's 25 Jan 2026 announcement -- names Haditha-to-Baniyas explicitly, ties it to the Basra-Haditha trunk as launch point. (2) Iraq Business News, 2026-01-28, sourced directly to the Ministry of Oil -- reports the minister-chaired implementation-plan review; independent origin from MEES (different byline/outlet, same week, not a wire reprint). (3) The National (UAE), 2026-05-01 -- independent confirmation that the Ministry's plan includes a Haditha-to-Baniyas branch alongside the Aqaba branch. (4) Peregraf (Iraqi Kurdish outlet), 2026-07-15 -- first-person quote from the sitting oil minister confirming the branch and naming the study consortium; independent of the Reuters-sourced July pack. (5) Pipeline Technology Journal / IraqiNews (Fishkhabur article), July 2026, both ultimately citing the same 5 Jul cabinet statement/Reuters wire -- treated as ONE corroborating thread, not counted twice toward independence, but used to source the concrete-step (HOA/NDA) detail. ina.iq (Iraqi News Agency) evidence item was fetched but returned a Cloudflare bot-challenge page on direct read (no live text retrieved) -- consistent with the consolidator's own flag that it was 'not independently re-read beyond substring verification'; not relied on for any value here, kept only in the verifications list as a documented non-independent/unconfirmed attempt.

Capacity, Length, Diameter, and Cost intentionally left blank: no source gives figures specific to this branch. The ~2 million bpd figure floated in Peregraf/AP coverage is for the combined Basra-Fishkhabur-Ceyhan network under study, not attributed to the Baniyas branch alone, so it was not used to populate Capacity (avoiding a false-precision orphan value). EndState/Province for Baniyas left blank -- none of the sources used here state the Syrian governorate (Tartous), and I did not want to borrow that fact from the existing P0546 Kirkuk-Baniyas row without an independent citation of my own. Tier set to medium: sponsor/endpoints are corroborated at green/high (2+ independent sources, one a direct ministerial quote), but the qualifying 'concrete step' is a non-binding feasibility-study HOA rather than a construction/FID commitment, and all engineering specifics (route, length, diameter, capacity) remain fully unknown -- an appropriately early-stage 'proposed'/Pre-FID add, not a high-confidence one.
